content.title: Right heart catheterization and EMB (endomyocardial biopsy) recommendations
content.source_context: Clinical guideline page (ESC 2021) section on right heart catheterization and EMB

recommendations.recommendation: Right heart catheterization is recommended in patients with severe HF being evaluated for heart transplantation or MCS.
recommendations.notes: Used for assessment prior to heart transplantation or mechanical circulatory support (MCS).

recommendations.recommendation: Right heart catheterization should be considered in patients where HF is thought to be due to constrictive pericarditis, restrictive cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, and high output states.
recommendations.notes: Considered for differential diagnosis in these specific causes of HF.

recommendations.recommendation: Right heart catheterization should be considered in patients with probable pulmonary hypertension, assessed by echo in order to confirm the diagnosis and assess its reversibility before the correction of valve/structural heart disease.
recommendations.notes: Used to confirm pulmonary hypertension and evaluate reversibility prior to valve/structural correction.

recommendations.recommendation: Right heart catheterization may be considered in selected patients with HFpEF to confirm the diagnosis.
recommendations.notes: Selective use in HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) when diagnostic confirmation is needed.

recommendations.recommendation: EMB should be considered in patients with rapidly progressive HF despite standard therapy when there is a probability of a specific diagnosis, which can be confirmed only in myocardial samples.
recommendations.notes: Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) recommended when myocardial sampling is required to confirm a suspected specific diagnosis.
